extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys, agents, applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on types of U.S. patent applications, formal requirements (filing contents, provisional rules), correction of inventorship, cross-noting/priority notation, and application status and status-inquiry procedures for examination and docketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents (35 U.S.C. 111(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Such application shall include—(A) a specification as prescribed by section 112 of this title; and (B) a drawing as prescribed by section 113 of this title; (C) an oath by the applicant as prescribed by section 115 of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must be accompanied by the fee required by law; the fee and oath may be submitted after the specification and any required drawing are submitted within such period and under such conditions (including surcharge) as prescribed by the Director. Failure to submit fee and oath within prescribed period results in abandonment unless delay shown to be unavoidable or unintentional. The filing date is the date on which the specification and any required drawing are received in the PTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application requirements (35 U.S.C. 111(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application shall include a specification as prescribed by the first paragraph of section 112 and a drawing as prescribed by section 113; a claim is not required in a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must be accompanied by the fee (which may be submitted later under prescribed conditions). The filing date is the date the specification and drawings are received. Provisional applications are abandoned 12 months after filing if not converted or a nonprovisional is not timely filed; they are not entitled to right of priority or benefit of earlier U.S. filing dates under sections 119 or 120/121/365(c). Provisional may be treated as a nonprovisional upon timely request as prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of national/nonprovisional/provisional/international applications (37 CFR 1.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'national application', 'provisional application', 'nonprovisional application', and 'international application' for purposes of the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national application is a U.S. application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111 or which entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371. Provisional is a U.S. national application under 111(b). Nonprovisional is a U.S. national application filed under 111(a) or entering national stage under 371. An international application is one filed under the PCT prior to entering national processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences in treatment: national applications vs national stage applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprovisional and provisional are national applications; treatment of a national application under 35 U.S.C. 111 and a national stage application under 35 U.S.C. 371 are similar but not identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Restriction practice under MPEP §806+ applies to national applications under 111(a) while unity of invention practice under MPEP Chapter 1800 applies to national stage applications; notification practice differs (37 CFR 1.53(f) vs 1.495). Examiners and practitioners must note which regime applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types/classification of domestic national applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic national patent applications fall under utility (35 U.S.C. 101), plant (35 U.S.C. 161), and design (35 U.S.C. 171) patents and include original (nonprovisional), provisional, plant, design, reissue, divisional, continuation, CPA, and continuation-in-part applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized procedures for design and plant patents are treated in Chapters 1500 and 1600 respectively; CPA and CIP filing rules and applicable CFR sections are identified (e.g., 37 CFR 1.53(b)/(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole application (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application wherein the invention is presented as that of a single person is termed a sole application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to categorize inventive entity; contrasts with joint application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint application (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A joint application is one in which the invention is presented as that of two or more persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §605.07 for additional handling and requirements for joint inventorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48 (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of inventorship in an application is permitted by amendment under 35 U.S.C. 116, implemented by 37 CFR 1.48; 1.48(a)-(f) address different circumstances (error in executed oath/declaration, prosecution-caused inventorship change, adding/deleting inventors in provisional, automatic correction upon first executed oath/declaration or cover sheet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utilization of a request under 37 CFR 1.48 will generally correct inventorship in the application in which it is filed. 1.48(a) addresses errors in executed oath/declaration; 1.48(b) deletions after prosecution; 1.48(c) adding when claims amended to include previously unclaimed subject matter; 1.48(d)/(e) provisional adds/deletes; 1.48(f) automatic corrections upon certain filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.48(a) required elements for correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.48(a) an amendment to change inventorship requires: (1) a request to correct the inventorship that sets forth the desired change; (2) a statement from each person being added and each person being deleted that the error occurred without deceptive intention; (3) an oath or declaration by the actual inventor(s) as required by §1.63 or permitted by §§1.42, 1.43 or 1.47; (4) the processing fee set forth in §1.17(i); and (5) if an assignment was executed by any of the original named inventors, the written consent of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The error must have arisen without deceptive intention. The written consent of assignees is necessary if assignments exist; 1.48 does not limit assignees to those recorded in PTO records (investigate file for assignee evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of lack of deceptive intention
rubrics_metrics.description: Each person being added and each person being deleted must provide a statement that the inventorship error occurred without deceptive intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement may simply state that the error occurred without deceptive intention and need not be a verified statement. Waiver under 37 CFR 1.183 of this requirement is rare and will be granted only when facts unequivocally support the correction sought. If a party refuses or cannot be reached, waiver may be appropriate upon showing refusal or inability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration requirements when correcting inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 by each actual inventor must be presented; each inventor must provide a complete listing of all inventors in his/her oath or declaration; individual declarations must be submitted separately (not combined into one).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where first-filed executed oaths/declarations name different inventive entities and are filed on the same day, the application is considered to name the inventors named in both declarations and a new declaration including the entire inventive entity is required. When an executed declaration exists it governs over conflicting papers; where no executed declaration is submitted, each party identified on filing will be considered named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicting oaths/declarations and their effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If the first executed oaths/declarations filed name different inventive entities and are filed on the same day, the application will be considered to name the inventors in both declarations and a new oath/declaration including the entire inventive entity will be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An executed declaration governs conflicting application papers (e.g., a transmittal letter). If an executed declaration is never submitted and application papers conflict as to inventorship, each party identified as an inventor on filing will be considered named. Examiners should require a compliant new declaration when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 37 CFR 1.47 and 1.183 petitions in inventorship corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.47 can be used to meet oath/declaration requirements in certain circumstances (e.g., where an inventor refuses to cooperate) and 37 CFR 1.183 petitions may request waiver of requirements under 1.48 such as statements or reexecution of oaths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.47 is applicable to original oath/declaration supplies; 1.183 petitions are exceptional and evaluated strictly (e.g., In re Cooper, In re Hardee). When filing petitions concurrently with requests, all fees must be submitted and the Office of Petitions may decide on matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirements for 37 CFR 1.48 and related petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A processing fee under 37 CFR 1.48(a) is required; where waiver under 1.183 is requested related fees (processing fee + petition fee) are required; if multiple petitions are filed multiple fees apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate processing fee must be submitted in each application in which correction is requested. If the processing fee is not submitted or authorized the request will be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written consent of assignee for inventorship correction
rubrics_metrics.description: The written consent of every existing assignee of the original named inventors must be submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48(a)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent must indicate the signatory's authority to act for the assignee (or be signed by an appropriate official whose title is of record). The assignee must establish ownership per 37 CFR 3.73 and MPEP §324. If no assignee exists requester should affirmatively state that fact; silence will be presumed as no assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a 37 CFR 1.48 request will not be required (exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request under 37 CFR 1.48 will not be required where: (A) application will issue with correct inventorship based on allowed claims; (B) typographical/transliteration errors in spelling are discovered (notify Office, no new oath required); (C) inventor's name changed after filing; (D) court order under 35 U.S.C. 256 for correction of patent (submit to Certificate of Correction Division); (E) incorrect name rather than change of individual (petition under 1.182); (F)-(G) first-filed oaths/declarations or cover sheets filed on/after Dec 1, 1997 that set forth correct inventors under specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§605.04(g), 1481 and applicable CFRs for detailed handling. Use appropriate petitions or notifications in lieu of 1.48 when listed exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing applications and inventorship overlap for benefit (35 U.S.C. 120)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 120 permits a continuing application to claim the benefit of the filing date of a copending previously filed parent application provided there is inventorship overlap between the continuing application and the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventorship overlap is met if the inventive entity of the continuing application includes an inventor named in the parent application. Overlap need not be present on the date the continuing application is filed nor when the parent issues or becomes abandoned (example provided where election/restriction and later divisional maintain overlap). Changes in inventorship via 1.48 may jeopardize benefit claims; intervening references must be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-noting / Front page notation of prior U.S. applications (including provisionals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The front page of a printed patent identifies all prior applications for which benefits are claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365(c) in continuation-in-part, continuation, divisional, substitute, and reissue applications; examiners should review identifying data to ensure accuracy and presence in the specification or application data sheet per 37 CFR 1.78(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to a prior nonprovisional must include appropriate relationship (continuation, divisional, CIP). Preprinted PALM bib-data sheet entries should be checked and corrected if necessary; if applicant claims benefit to a provisional that itself claims priority to earlier apps, earlier apps should not be reflected on PALM because provisional is not entitled to priority of other applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM bib-data sheet verification and correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Where prior application data is preprinted on the PALM bib-data sheet the examiner should check that data for accuracy and initial the sheet when correct; corrections may be made by Technology Center technical support staff and a new sheet printed and scanned into the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data is silent as to existence of an assignee or prior application, assume no assignee/prior app and set forth that presumption in the decision to alert requesters to requirements. Examiner should initial 'VERIFIED' when information is correct or amended to be correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation in file wrapper when claiming foreign priority
rubrics_metrics.description: A PALM bib-data sheet should include the application number, country (or intellectual property authority), day, month, and year of each foreign application that the U.S. application is claiming priority of; examiner should check for accuracy and correct via Legal Examiner if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If certified copies of foreign applications have been received, information for each foreign application is to be entered on the PALM bib-data sheet. The front page and Official Gazette will refer to the claim of priority for those apps endorsed on the PALM sheet. Examiner must still indicate on Office action/PALM whether conditions of 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) or (f) have been met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration identification of foreign applications (37 CFR 1.63 & 1.76)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.63 requires that the oath or declaration must identify any foreign application for which a claim for priority is made pursuant to 37 CFR 1.55, specifying application number, country, day, month, and year, unless such information is supplied on an application data sheet in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure oath/declaration or ADS contains required foreign priority identifiers to support priority claims and proper front-page and file notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status definitions: New
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'new' application is a nonprovisional application that has not yet received an action by the examiner. An amendment filed prior to the first Office Action does not alter 'new' status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for docketing and expected examiner handling timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status definitions: Rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application which, during prosecution and before allowance, contains an unanswered examiner's action is designated as a 'rejected' application. Its status continues until applicant replies or it becomes abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor reply periods to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status definitions: Amended
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'amended' nonprovisional application is one that, having been acted on by the examiner, has in turn been acted on by the applicant in reply (e.g., election, traverse, or amendment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended applications are expected to be taken up promptly for further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status definitions: Allowed or in Issue
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'allowed' nonprovisional application or an application 'in issue' is one which, having been examined, is passed to issue as a patent, subject to payment of the issue fee. Status continues from notice of allowance until withdrawn from issue, issued, or abandoned per 37 CFR 1.316.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files of allowed applications are sent to Office of Patent Publication (IFW processing referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status definitions: Abandoned
rubrics_metrics.description: An abandoned application is one removed from the Office docket of pending applications through formal abandonment by applicant (or assignee), failure to take appropriate action during prosecution, failure to pay issue fee, or (for provisional) lapse after 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment can be formal or result from inaction; for provisionals see MPEP §711.03(c) and 35 U.S.C. 111(b)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status definitions: Incomplete
rubrics_metrics.description: An application that is not entitled to a filing date (e.g., lacking essential parts) is termed an incomplete application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §506 and §601.01(d)-(g) for details on essential parts and filing date entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status inquiry timing and applicant guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when applicants should inquire about application status: e.g., status inquiry appropriate when Notice of Allowance not received within three months from receipt of PTOL-37; amended applications expected to be taken up within two months of examiner receipt so applicant should not inquire until 5-6 months with no response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to use PAIR for status checks. Stamped postcard receipts for replies serve as prima facie proof of receipt; timely reply proof may obviate petitions to revive in certain circumstances (see 37 CFR 1.113).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of status letters by Technology Centers (TC) and examiner support
rubrics_metrics.description: TCs will receive status letters and route them to designated locations for action; TC representative determines nature of request and whether requester is entitled to information using PALM Intranet and may review application file as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps include: use PALM Intranet to determine status, review new application dates, tracking systems, consult with SPE or examiner, review file when necessary; reply by phone/fax/mail as appropriate; note replies on status letter; use Status Letter Database and associate the correspondence with application file (including abandoned ones).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Congressional and other official inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence and inquiries from the White House, Members of Congress, embassies, and heads of Executive departments and agencies normally are cleared through the Office of International Relations and/or the Office of Congressional Relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such inquiries should be referred initially to staff in the appropriate office for uniform handling and compliance with Department of Commerce directives; transmit immediately to the relevant office and notify staff by phone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of inventorship correction on benefit claims and intervening references
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant or denial of a request under 37 CFR 1.48 may result in loss of inventorship overlap between a parent and continuing application and consequent inability to claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120; intervening references must be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a 1.48 request is denied in a final agency action, the examiner must determine whether a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) or (g) is appropriate. If request was entered and dismissed for correctable defect, treating 102(f)/(g) may be premature. For allowed applications where issue fee paid prior to entry of 1.48 request, if request is dismissed/denied, application must be withdrawn from issue to permit correction; if granted, withdrawal is unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and office record updates when correction granted
rubrics_metrics.description: When a request under 37 CFR 1.48(a)-(c) is granted, the examiner will acknowledge additions/deletions using form paragraph 2.14 or 2.14.01 in the next Office communication; PALM records must be revised, a corrected filing receipt issued, and bib-data sheet changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction should be noted on the original oath/declaration (e.g., write 'See Paper No. __ for inventorship corrections'). For IFW processing see the IFW Manual. Form paragraph templates include examiner notes and bracketed insertion points for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirements for inventorship correction and related timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Although 37 CFR 1.48 does not contain a diligence requirement, once an inventorship error is discovered timeliness requirements under 37 CFR 1.116 and 37 CFR 1.312 apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act promptly upon discovering inventorship errors; delayed filings may impact revival options and benefit claims. For allowed applications, pay attention to issue fee timing relative to 1.48 requests.
